about.title: Studio
about.lead: AURA360LAB is an architecture, interior design and 3D visualization studio founded in 2025 and based in Marrakech.
about.storyHeadline: From a story to a space.
story: AURA 360 LAB was born from a simple idea: architecture should have a feeling of its own.

We see every project as a dialogue between a place and the people connected to it. Whether it is a home, a hospitality space, a workplace, or a small detail, there is always something to discover... A story waiting to be told.

We are interested in spaces that feel personal rather than simply designed. Spaces where a material invites you to touch it, where light changes throughout the day, and where a crafted detail gives character to an ordinary moment.
We don't seek to make every project look like AURA. We seek to make every project feel like itself.
That is where its unique AURA begins.
about.storyImageAlt: Saad Benlyamani and Mansour Kammoun, founders of AURA360LAB, in the studio
vision: We believe architecture is not only what we see. It is what we feel, touch, hear, and remember.

At AURA 360 LAB, we explore the relationship between space, material, light, and human experience. We design environments where every texture, shadow, opening, and detail contributes to a deeper sense of place.
Our approach is rooted in local materials, craftsmanship, and experimentation, combining architectural thinking with an attentive understanding of how spaces are actually experienced.
about.teamIntro: AURA360LAB was founded in 2025 by two architects.

bios.saad: Trained in architecture in Tunisia and professionally shaped in Morocco, Saad brings a strategic and client-centred vision to AURA 360 LAB. He approaches every project like a carefully considered move—understanding its needs, anticipating possibilities, and transforming the client's vision into thoughtful, tailor-made architecture.
bios.mansour: A Tunisian architect specializing in architectural design and 3D visualization, Mansour has developed an approach in which technical mastery serves emotion and spatial storytelling. Named North Africa's Best ArchViz Student in 2019, he explores light, materials and proportions to create spaces that feel refined, coherent and timeless.
